articles.title: La nueva realidad del baloncesto europeo: "Seis millones de cláusula es mucho, pero igual se paga"
articles.standfirst: Luis Arbalejo, director deportivo del Valencia Basket, analiza los cambios en el mercado por la llegada de nuevos ricos y la ambición de propietarios millonarios
articles.summary: Luis Arbalejo, director deportivo del Valencia Basket, analiza los cambios en el mercado por la llegada de nuevos ricos y la ambición de propietarios millonarios
articles.body: En el verano del baloncesto europeo nadie ha sufrido más las consecuencias de la nueva realidad del mercado que el Valencia Basket. El proyecto que se proclamó campeón de la Liga Endesa y alcanzó la Final Four de la Euroliga por primera vez en la historia del club se desmembró ante el pago de cláusulas de rescisión. De esa manera salieron el líder espiritual Pedro Martínez y estrellas como Jaime Pradilla (ambos con rumbo al Real Madrid por un millón de euros y 1,5 millones, respectivamente), Jean Montero (a Olympiacos por medio millón) y Brancou Badio (al Panathinaikos por 1,5 millones). Así que, intentando que no se repita algo así, el club intenta blindarse y ha establecido alguna cláusula de hasta seis millones. Otra cosa es que eso intimide a los grandes presupuestos de la Euroliga. La entrada del Dubái Basketball y el Hapoel Tel Aviv se ha unido a la ambición de propietarios con mucho dinero en los bolsillos, como los del Olympiacos y el Panathinaikos provocando una tremenda inflación. Hay clubes a los que no hay cláusulas que se les resistan y eso se asume en Valencia. "Hay cláusulas que quizás no son disuasorias para un presidente del Panathinaikos o un propietario del Hapoel Tel Aviv o el Dubái, que están pagando lo que pagan", asegura Luis Arbalejo, director deportivo de la entidad taronja. El club de los emitatos acaba de pagar 2,6 millones de dólares para sacar a Thomas Walkup del Olympiacos y, a sus 33 años y con un rol en principio secundario, le ha puesto un contrato de 9,6 millones por tres campañas. "En el baloncesto, las cláusulas, por muy altas que sean, todavía no son disuasorias. No sé hasta qué punto llegaremos. Antes, un millón era mucho y ahora mucho, quizás sean cinco o seis millones, pero es que quizá se paguen", analiza Arbalejo sobre el nuevo escenario del baloncesto europeo.

articles.title: NBA Expansion to Las Vegas, Seattle, Europe Reportedly to be Addressed by Board of Governors
articles.summary: The NBA's expansion plans may take a small step forward this week.
articles.body:
The NBA's expansion plans may take a small step forward this week.

David Aldridge and Joe Vardon of The Athletic reported the league's Board of Governors "is expected to continue to address two areas of potential expansion: the proposed NBA Europe deal and the potential domestic expansions into the Seattle and Las Vegas markets."

The board is opening its fall meeting Monday in New York City.

It's unlikely to vote on expanding into Seattle and Las Vegas, so nothing official on that front is imminent. The NBA is still weighing a number of factors including ownership candidates, basketball-related infrastructure, and the wider repercussions of adding up to two teams.

The NBA's venture into Europe is also far from his final form.

"The NBA has vetted multiple candidates for the proposed 16-team league, including 12 permanent members, with bids running from $500 million to as much as $1 billion per team, according to sources with knowledge of the discussions," per Aldridge and Vardon.

The presence of the EuroLeague is another component at play. EuroLeague owners reportedly have their own meeting scheduled in October to discuss partnering with the NBA or remaining independent and in effect being direct competition.

NBA commissioner Adam Silver has set a goal of opening play in Europe by the 2027-28 season.

If nothing else, perhaps the Board of Governors meeting will help to solidify a clearer timeline, especially as it relates to domestic expansion.

articles.title: New Celtics Rumors on 1st-Round Lottery Pick Signing Contract, Updated Roster & Depth Chart
articles.summary: Ahead of the start of NBA training camp, the Boston Celtics reportedly added some youth to their roster.
articles.body:
Ahead of the start of NBA training camp, the Boston Celtics reportedly added some youth to their roster.

Per Michael Scotto of HoopsHype, the Celtics have agreed to a deal with former Sacramento Kings guard Devin Carter, who was the No. 13 pick in the 2024 NBA draft. Carter reportedly will be competing for a roster or two-way spot in training camp.

Following the addition of Carter, Boston's updated depth chart looks like this:

After a nondescript rookie campaign, Carter appeared to still be in Sacramento's future plans when the team exercised his third-year option prior to the 2025-26 season. He played in 38 games during his sophomore campaign with 12 starts, averaging 8.9 points, 3.3 rebounds and 2.7 assists in 18.4 minutes of action. He set a career-high with 29 points on six three-pointers in a win over the Golden State Warriors in April. However, the Kings traded him to the Atlanta Hawks during the 2026 draft, and he was waived last week.

The Celtics already have a strong backcourt with two-way star point guard Derrick White and sixth man Payton Pritchard. The team also added veteran floor general Mike Conley over the offseason to provide extra depth.

Still, Boston will have to replace the production of star shooting guard Jaylen Brown after trading him to the Philadelphia 76ers. Third-year guard Baylor Scheierman is expected to take his spot in the starting lineup, though he averaged just 5.5 points across 77 games and 20 starts last season.

Carter will have the chance to prove his worth during training camp as the Celtics try to ensure they have what it takes to return to title contention during the 2026-27 campaign.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark Talks Design Process for Nike Signature Shoe in Video, Colorways Revealed in Photo
articles.summary: Less than a month out from its worldwide release, Nike pulled back the curtain on the signature shoe for Indiana Fever star Caitlin Clark.
articles.body:
Less than a month out from its worldwide release, Nike pulled back the curtain on the signature shoe for Indiana Fever star Caitlin Clark.

The company released a video Monday outlining the design process behind the Caitlin 1.

For her part, Clark wanted a shoe that would help her make quick cuts and wriggle free from defenders on the perimeter. Alex Zerzan, a product line manager for Nike Basketball, also recounted how the three-time All-Star wanted "stuff that I've never seen before."

Watch: Sophie Cunningham's viral football kick

There will be at least six different colorways for the Caitlin 1s:

For nearly 20 years, WNBA players had little to no representation within the sneaker world. That changed when Puma signed two-time MVP Breanna Stewart and gave her a signature shoe in 2022.

The Las Vegas Aces' A'ja Wilson, New York Liberty's Sabrina Ionescu and Atlanta Dream's Angel Reese have all received dedicated sneaker and apparel lines since then.

The Caitlin 1s are arguably the most anticipated of the bunch. Her fans have been eagerly awaiting the day ever since she broke through on a national stage as a junior at Iowa in 2022-23.

Beyond the design aesthetics, Nike sought to craft a shoe to Clark's specifications and on-court needs.

"The result is a signature model built around the specific demands of Clark's game, helping her play with the speed, range and unpredictability that have defined her rise, while inviting athletes everywhere to unlock new dimensions of their own game," the company said .

Clark has been wearing the shoe throughout the 2026 WNBA season. That has coincided with a strong rebound from her injury-marred 2025. She's averaging 22.5 points and 8.4 assists while setting personal highs in field-goal percentage (45.6) and three-point percentage (37.3).

The Caitlin 1s will hit stores on Oct. 1.

articles.title: 'Villain' Dillon Brooks Reveals Mike Tyson Technique He Learned and Addresses Weight Loss
articles.summary: Dillon Brooks held a basketball camp for kids and teenagers in Arizona over the weekend, and greeted them with a stare.
articles.body:
Dillon Brooks held a basketball camp for kids and teenagers in Arizona over the weekend, and greeted them with a stare.

Per Doug Haller of The Athletic, "When a slimmed-down Brooks first walked into the gym, while the 350 campers chanted his name, he stopped and stared—a breathing/focus exercise he does before games, something he took from former heavyweight champ Mike Tyson. Then he ran through the campers and gave them high fives. (Told that he looks lighter, Brooks said any weight loss was not done purposely, and he would add a few pounds now that he's back in the States. NBA training camps begin later this month. 'I feel great,' he said.)"

Brooks, 30, signed a three-year, $73 million extension with the Phoenix Suns this offseason after averaging a career-high 20.2 points per game across 56 contests. And of course, he continued to live up to his reputation as one of the NBA's most prominent pests.

"As a human being, you have good, and you have a little bit of bad, a little bit of villainy," he told Haller. "It's always in moderation, but I feel like people kind of resonate with that. A villain doesn't have to be always bad. There's good in it, as well. It's the hard work. It's the relentlessness to be the best at what you want to be, and I try to instill that in myself and try to showcase it in a different way."

Golden State Warriors star point guard Stephen Curry has done it all in his legendary career, and now he will be the subject of a documentary following his journey to 4,000 three-pointers.

Distributed by Disney, Portrait of an Artist: Stephen Curry will be released exclusively in IMAX theaters on Oct. 9, and a new trailer for the film dropped on Monday:

Curry eclipsed 4,000 career three-pointers in a win over the Sacramento Kings during the 2024-25 campaign.

"This film is all about capturing Steph Curry, an athlete and artist who is always chasing a new masterpiece," director Gotham Chopra said in a statement . "With the court as his canvas, we wanted to show the world the relentless creativity and discipline that drives one of the greatest to ever play the game. We are thrilled to be able to share this film in IMAX with audiences across the country."

Curry will enter the 2026-27 season with 4,248 career three-pointers, so it will be fun to see how high he can extend his all-time record before he hangs it up.

articles.title: Campazzo pone fecha al nuevo Real Madrid: "Ahora empieza lo bueno"
articles.standfirst: El base pide paciencia y pese a las buenas sensaciones asegura que tienen "mucho margen de mejora"
articles.summary: El base pide paciencia y pese a las buenas sensaciones asegura que tienen "mucho margen de mejora"
articles.body: Facundo Campazzo analizó el proceso de transformación del Real Madrid de Pedro Martínez. El base argentino admite que el equipo todavía está en plena adaptación a las nuevas ideas del técnico y avisa de que la mejor versión llegará con el paso del tiempo: "A medida que pasen los meses y los partidos vamos a ir mejorando". Así lo explicó en una entrevista que concedió a los medios del club blanco. Cuatro amistosos han servido para tomar contacto con el nuevo proyecto, con una derrota ante el Río Breogán y victorias frente a Baskonia, La Laguna Tenerife y Unicaja. El cambio de ritmo y la búsqueda de amenaza ofensiva desde los primeros segundos marcan la propuesta de Pedro Martínez. "Estamos viviendo ese proceso de equivocarnos mucho, pero sobre la marcha intentamos mejorar y no cometer los mismos errores", reconoce Campazzo. El margen para aprender se reduce ahora al mínimo. El viernes llega el primer gran examen con las semifinales de la Supercopa de la Euroliga ante el Dubai Basketball. El Real Madrid, subcampeón de Europa, tendrá a tiro su primer título del curso en un torneo en el que también se medirán Olympiacos y Fenerbahce. "Creo que los amistosos nos ayudaron muchísimo para medirnos y ahora empieza lo bueno, la competición", asegura el argentino. Campazzo tiene claro que el objetivo no cambia: "Es un nuevo año, con los mismos objetivos de siempre". El desafío será trasladar cuanto antes al parquet las nuevas ideas del técnico y conseguir que un equipo con varias caras nuevas alcance la velocidad de crucero. "Tenemos el primer título en unos días y es una buena prueba, con equipos de primer nivel", sentencia. Walter Tavares comparte el optimismo de su compañero. El pívot caboverdiano destaca las buenas sensaciones de un equipo que todavía tiene recorrido por delante: "Estamos teniendo muy buenas sensaciones y todavía tenemos mucho margen de mejora". Con las llegadas de Max Shulga, Timothé Luwawu-Cabarrot, Mikael Jantunen, Jaime Pradilla, Damian Jones y Olivier Sarr, además del estreno de Pedro Martínez en el banquillo, el nuevo Madrid pide tiempo para encontrar su identidad. "Creo que con el tiempo vamos a ir perfeccionando las cosas, pero vamos por muy buen camino"

articles.title: Kawhi Leonard trade to Raptors reportedly will be completed after NBA punishes Clippers for breaking salary cap rules
articles.summary: The Raptors originally agreed to a trade for Leonard in June as the Clippers did not want to sign the 35-year-old to a contract extension.
articles.body:
The previously agreed-upon trade between the Los Angeles Clippers and Toronto Raptors involving Kawhi Leonard will go through, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

Leonard returns to Toronto, where he won the 2019 NBA championship, in exchange for 2031 and 2033 unprotected first-round selections, and a 2027 first-round swap. The Clippers also receive second-round picks in 2030 and 2033, along with forward Brandon Ingram and guard Gradey Dick .

The Clippers will still get the two first-rounders from the Raptors despite the NBA stripping the team of five first-round selections (their own picks in 2031 and 2033, along with 2029, 2030 and 2032 picks).

Losing the draft picks was part of the league's penalty for its investigation of the Clippers for allegations that Leonard received impermissible benefits, including being paid $28 million for a "no-show job," as a way of circumventing the NBA salary cap.

Ingram, 29, averaged 21.5 points, 4.8 rebounds and 3.7 assists while shooting 38% on 3-pointers after being acquired from the New Orleans Pelicans . Shortly after joining Toronto, he signed a three-year, $120 million contract extension .

Dick, who turns 23 in November, is going into his fourth NBA season. He was the Raptors' 2023 first-round pick (No. 13 overall) out of Kansas. After averaging 14.4 points and shooting 35% on 3s in his second season, Dick's scoring dropped to 6.0 points per game and 30% shooting from long range last season.

"As I return to Toronto, I am focused on what I can control, closing this chapter, and moving forward with a clean slate," Leonard said in a statement released after the NBA handed down its punishment to the Clippers.

The seven-time All-Star is expected to sign a contract extension with the Raptors, which the Clippers were not interested in doing. He is in the final year of his contract, which is set to pay him $50 million . Last season, Leonard averaged a career-high 27.9 points in 65 games with 6.4 rebounds, 3.6 assists and 1.9 steals. He shot nearly 39% on 445 3-point attempts.

Clippers, Raptors originally agreed to Leonard trade in June

The trade of Leonard to the Raptors was originally agreed upon in late June , though wasn't expected to become official until July 6 when the NBA's moratorium on transactions ended.

However, the deal was put on hold amid the NBA's investigation into the Clippers allegedly evading the league's salary cap while signing Leonard to a three-year, $103 million free-agent contract in July 2019. Both the Clippers and Raptors agreed that the trade wouldn't be completed until the league's probe was completed.

NBA commissioner Adam Silver stated during a press conference during the Las Vegas Summer League that the decision to delay the trade was not made by the league , but by the Clippers and Raptors.

NBA issues harsh penalties for Clippers avoiding salary cap rules

In addition to the Clippers being stripped of five first-round picks, team owner Steve Ballmer was fined $30 million and is suspended "from all league and team activities for one year." President of basketball operations Lawrence Frank received a six-month suspension without pay. Receiving a one-year suspension without pay was president of business operations Gillian Zucker.

Leonard himself was also fined $700,000 by the league. And Leonard's uncle and business adviser, Dennis Robertson , was also banned from engaging in any future business dealings with the NBA.

On Sunday night, Ballmer released a statement saying he accepts the NBA's punishment and won't pursue a legal challenge, as he'd previously indicated.

articles.title: Kawhi Leonard Traded to Raptors After Clippers Investigation, New NBA Rumors Reveal Full Details
articles.summary: The trade sending star forward Kawhi Leonard from the Los Angeles Clippers to the Toronto Raptors reportedly has officially been processed on Monday.
articles.body:
The trade sending star forward Kawhi Leonard from the Los Angeles Clippers to the Toronto Raptors reportedly has officially been processed on Monday.

ESPN's Shams Charania reported that the Clippers signed off on the trade after spending the last two weeks working through the logistics of their punishment following an NBA investigation:

Toronto obtained Leonard in a trade with Los Angeles while sending out Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick, two first-round draft picks, two second-round selections and a pick swap on June 30.

However, the trade was put on hold while the NBA investigated Leonard and the Clippers for circumventing salary cap rules. The league eventually announced penalties for Leonard and the Clippers on Sept. 2.

Ballmer announced on Sunday night that he was accepting the league's punishment:

On June 30, ESPN's Shams Charania reported that Leonard's representatives informed interested teams on the trade market that he would only be willing to sign an extension with the Raptors and envisioned ending his career in Toronto.

The new contract doesn't come as a shock, as Charania also reported July 6 that Leonard and the Raptors were "expected to start" discussions on an extension following the trade.

The seven-time All-Star is beginning his second stint as a member of the Raptors organization, previously suiting up for them during the 2018-19 season.

Leonard exceeded expectations in his initial year on the Raptors, helping them finish with a 58-24 record before capturing their first championship in franchise history.

He averaged 30.5 points per game while connecting on 49.0 percent of his shot attempts in the playoffs with Toronto, earning Finals MVP honors after taking down the Golden State Warriors in six games.

Leonard eventually signed with the Clippers during the ensuing offseason.

The 35-year-old is coming off a dominant 2025-26 campaign in Los Angeles, averaging a career-high 27.9 points per game. He also recorded 6.4 rebounds, 3.6 assists and 1.9 steals on a nightly basis while finishing the year with 50.5/38.7/89.2 shooting splits.

Toronto compiled a 46-36 record and earned a playoff berth last season led by Scottie Barnes, who earned his second career All-Star nod and finished No. 5 in Defensive Player of the Year voting .

With Barnes and Leonard leading the way, the Raptors are expecting to contend for a championship in 2027.

articles.title: Luz verde de la NBA al bombazo del verano: Kawhi Leonard vuelve a los Raptors
articles.standfirst: El alero deja los Clippers y pone rumbo a Toronto, donde ganó el anillo en 2019
articles.summary: El alero deja los Clippers y pone rumbo a Toronto, donde ganó el anillo en 2019
articles.body: La NBA da luz verde al bombazo del verano: Kawhi Leonard volverá a los Toronto Raptors después de que Clippers y Raptors hayan acordado finalmente completar el traspaso que se había quedado en el aire según ha adelantado en exclusiva Shams Charania, de ESPN. Ambos equipos tienen previsto ahora formalizar la operación, que inicialmente habían pactado el pasado 30 de junio. El acuerdo quedó paralizado durante semanas por la investigación de la NBA a los Clippers por una posible vulneración de las normas del límite salarial. La Liga terminó imponiendo un castigo histórico a la franquicia angelina: cinco primeras rondas del draft, 30 millones de dólares de multa y un año de suspensión para Steve Ballmer, propietario del equipo. Con el traspaso ya desbloqueado, los Clippers recibirán a Brandon Ingram y Gradey Dick, además de dos primeras rondas sin protección, un intercambio de primeras rondas y dos segundas rondas. Una operación de enorme calado que transforma por completo el futuro inmediato de ambas franquicias. Leonard regresa así a la ciudad donde se convirtió en leyenda. En 2019 llevó a los Raptors hasta el primer anillo de su historia, antes de abandonar Toronto ese mismo verano rumbo a Los Ángeles. Siete años después, el círculo se cierra con un regreso inesperado y uno de los grandes movimientos de la NBA.

Longtime NBA forward Taj Gibson is moving on to the next chapter of his career.

On Monday, Gibson announced his retirement from the NBA after 17 seasons. ESPN's Shams Charania reported that he will be joining the Chicago Bulls as an assistant coach under first-year head coach Tiago Splitter.

Gibson was drafted 26th overall by the Bulls in 2009, and he endeared himself to the franchise as a do-everything "glue guy" who contributed on both ends of the floor. He also suited up for the Oklahoma City Thunder, Minnesota Timberwolves, New York Knicks, Washington Wizards, Detroit Pistons, Charlotte Hornets and Memphis Grizzlies.

New York Knicks star center Karl-Anthony Towns, who teamed with Gibson on the Timberwolves, gave him a shout-out on social media:

articles.title: Caitlin Clark, Angel Reese's Final Box Score Stats from Gold-Medal Run at 2026 FIBA World Cup
articles.summary: The United States' gold-medal-winning roster was loaded with WNBA superstars during the 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup.
articles.body:
The United States' gold-medal-winning roster was loaded with WNBA superstars during the 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup.

Two of those stars in Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese have been generating headlines since they entered the league in the 2024 WNBA draft. While neither of them was the go-to offensive option for the Americans during the tournament, they still put up solid numbers.

Here is a look at the per-game averages throughout the run to the gold medal for Clark and Reese:

Clark and Reese impressed for stretches, but it was Breanna Stewart who stood out as the best player for the Red, White and Blue. The forward led the team in scoring (12.8) and rebounds (7.3) per game and put the Americans on her back during Sunday's 97-79 victory over France in the gold-medal game.

France actually built a double-digit lead in the second quarter before Stewart took over on her way to a double-double of 22 points, 10 rebounds and four assists. Whenever the United States needed a key basket, it consistently turned her way as a matchup nightmare.

That's not to say Clark and Reese weren't important as well.

Clark provided a spark off the bench with 12 points in the gold-medal game. She also led the team in assists per game and was a driver of the offense for the second unit.

As for Reese, she played excellent interior defense and led the team in blocks per game. She was also on the floor for stretches when the Americans seized control Sunday and provided some of that important defense in key possessions.

Clark and Reese were primary reasons the second unit thrived at times in the World Cup, and the latter discussed playing together.

"We've played against each other so many times. I'm sure we know each other's game like the back of each other's hand," Reese told reporters . "So just easily dishing it off to her. She dishes off to me. She knows my spots. I kinda got one to her today, maybe two. So it's fun. We just continue to build chemistry because we know we're gonna be USA teammates for a while."

They're now World Cup gold medalists together.

articles.title: New Kawhi Leonard Rumors Reveal Trade Kicker Update for Raptors-Clippers Deal, Impact on Salary Cap
articles.summary: Kawhi Leonard is returning to the Toronto Raptors and reportedly did some financial maneuvering to make the trade work.
articles.body:
Kawhi Leonard is returning to the Toronto Raptors and reportedly did some financial maneuvering to make the trade work.

ESPN's Shams Charania reported Monday the Los Angeles Clippers are sending Leonard to the Raptors in exchange for Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick, two unprotected first-round picks, one first-round pick swap and two second-round picks.

Charania and Bobby Marks also reported that Leonard waived his 15 percent trade kicker that was worth $7.45 million in order to "facilitate the trade" that leaves Toronto "pressed at the first apron."

Notably, Los Angeles agreed to trade Leonard to the Raptors back in June. However, the trade was paused during an ongoing investigation of Leonard and the Clippers.

The NBA announced in September an independent investigation found Los Angeles engaged in "a pattern of misconduct and multiple significant rules violations" and punished the team and player "for violating the salary cap circumvention rules contained in the league's Collective Bargaining Agreement."

The punishments included a $30 million fine for the Clippers, the forfeiture of five first-round draft picks, a one-year suspension for team governor Steve Ballmer and a $700,000 fine for Leonard.

While the Clippers initially said they would challenge the penalties, Ballmer announced Sunday the team decided to comply instead and paid the fine in an effort to move forward.

Completing this trade is a big part of moving forward, and Los Angeles getting significant draft capital back in return for Leonard should help its rebuilding efforts in the future after losing so many picks in the punishments.

As for the Raptors, they are getting a future Hall of Famer and franchise icon back in the deal.

While Leonard was previously with Toronto for just one season, he led the team to the championship as the 2019 NBA Finals MVP. His playoff run included brilliant individual play against the powerhouse Golden State Warriors in those Finals and a buzzer-beater to win Game 7 of a second-round series against the Philadelphia 76ers.

He provides far more starpower to a Raptors team that could use some outside of Scottie Barnes.

Toronto took the Cleveland Cavaliers to seven games in the first round of last season's playoffs with Barnes and RJ Barrett leading the way. It still has those two, and they should see far more open looks with the defensive attention Leonard draws on a nightly basis.

The Raptors may not be in position to win another title with Leonard, but they will be far more formidable in the Eastern Conference picture.

articles.title: The Kawhi Leonard trade to Toronto is finally happening. What does the future hold for the Raptors?
articles.summary: While the basketball reasons for acquiring Leonard are no-brainers, the off-court noise puts this move under a national scope that won't go away anytime soon...
articles.body:
Seven years after Kawhi Leonard led the Toronto Raptors to an unprecedented NBA championship, the superstar forward is once again a resident of the North.

On Monday, less than 24 hours after Clippers governor Steve Ballmer publicly took ownership of the salary cap circumvention scandal involving Leonard and four companies — and less than 24 hours before commissioner Adam Silver is set to publicly speak following the Board of Governors meetings in New York — both teams finalized the terms of the long-awaited blockbuster deal . Toronto is sending Brandon Ingram , Gradey Dick , a pair of unprotected first-round picks in 2031 and 2033, a pick swap in 2027 and two future seconds (2030 and 2033).

If that feels like a premium, it's because it is — but for good reason. While it's not particularly common that superstars are traded in their mid-to-late 30s ( Jimmy Butler , Kevin Durant and Damian Lillard come to mind), the need for a player of Leonard's ilk, adjacent to Toronto's status within the Eastern Conference hierarchy, necessitated an aggressive move. From a shot profile standpoint, Leonard's caliber is hard to come by (2009 Kobe Bryant is the closest you'll find, which makes sense given the ability and aura). By several metrics (take your pick: fifth in PER, third in DARKO, fifth in VORP, fourth in ESPN's Net Points WAR), Leonard's 2025-26 campaign was that of a Tier 1 talent, production augmented by the fact he was available for nearly 70 games.

It became more apparent down the stretch in Toronto last season that, while Scottie Barnes is Leonard's heir apparent (both from a defensive efficiency and offensive growth standpoint), the Raptors would be much better suited for long-term success pairing the former alongside Leonard's skill set. Ingram wasn't a hand-in-glove fit for that role, an underlying factor in their first-round elimination at the hands of the Cleveland Cavaliers .

But Leonard's arrival shouldn't be viewed through the lens of some outside savior. Toronto is a well-coached unit on both sides of the ball that cherishes possessions and sticks to its tentpoles. The Raptors finished in the bottom five in high-leverage minutes during the regular season and the bottom half of first-round playoff participants , an impressive feat assuming every postseason possession is high-stakes (in other words, the Raptors don't throw games away). This is a team that finished 10th in net rating, seventh in defensive efficiency and a sliver outside the top 10 in offense. Swapping out Ingram for Leonard naturally makes them a better team — Bball Index has their projected starting five with an efficiency that would have ranked among the top five among high-usage pairings last season — but this was a group already on the cusp of a jump in status.

Expect a smooth transition with Leonard's 95th percentile impact as a Clipper in the Raptors' fast-break attack (No. 1 in frequency with a bottom-10 efficiency). His playmaking prowess meshes well with the likes of Immanuel Quickley , RJ Barrett and Barnes, the outside shooting should improve a unit that finished 25th in 3-point rate and his gravity will open more opportunities for his new teammates. Defensively, we don't need to go into that much detail with Barnes' All-Defensive presence and Leonard's name alone — say goodbye to your perimeter plans.

In any case, however, while the basketball reasons for acquiring Leonard are no-brainers, the off-court noise puts this move under a national scope that won't go away anytime soon.

Leonard's part in the Clippers ' wrongdoings — regardless of who you pin the bulk of the blame on — has created an unfortunate cloud that might spark more distractions than necessary. And even if he signs an extension in Toronto, one has to wonder what his leadership looks like within a new regime under a coach that demands accountability at all levels. It wasn't too long ago that Leonard's frustrations with losing reached public levels to a point where Ty Lue had to push back in the media. What if things don't get off to a smooth start in a world where the New York Knicks reign supreme?

All of these are questions worth asking, especially after executing a trade of this magnitude. Brilliant player on the floor, questionable ethics off it and the unknown gray area that is now the Raptors' present — and potentially future.

articles.title: 17-year, $92.3 million NBA veteran Taj Gibson hangs up basketball sneakers in a latest move, gets new role in Bulls
articles.summary: NBA News: Taj Gibson has closed the book on a 17-year NBA career; however, he's not going far from the game. The 41-year-old forward announced his retirement on.
articles.body: Taj Gibson has closed the book on a 17-year NBA career; however, he's not going far from the game. The 41-year-old forward announced his retirement on Monday, then turned right around and joined Tiago Splitter's coaching staff in Chicago, the same city where his career began back in 2009.His final months as a player were a series of jerseys. Memphis traded him to New Orleans last week, and the Pelicans waived him almost immediately. Instead of chasing a 15th roster spot somewhere else, Gibson picked the bench in a different sense, choosing to return to the franchise that drafted him.Taj Gibson announces retirementTaj Gibson made the call himself; he posted the news on social media rather than waiting for a team release. "It's the beginning of a new chapter," he wrote. He described walking away with no regrets. “After 31 years of basketball, I can walk away with no regrets, knowing I left everything on the floor. God has truly blessed me.”Across 1,012 career games, Gibson averaged 8.3 points and 5.7 rebounds, suiting up for eight franchises total: the Bulls, Oklahoma City, Minnesota, New York, Detroit, Charlotte, Memphis and briefly New Orleans on paper. He was a 6-foot-9 forward taken in the first round of the 2009 draft, and he spent his first seven-plus seasons defending for Tom Thibodeau's Chicago teams.Taj Gibson gets new NBA role in Chicago BullsGibson's new title is assistant coach, and he'll report to Splitter, who was hired in June. He joins a staff that already includes Wes Unseld Jr., Blake Ahearn, Jamelle McMillan, Rex Kalamian and Jonah Herscu. Some fans wanted a playing reunion once New Orleans cut him loose, but Chicago's front office, led by Bryson Graham, went a different direction. Handing him a coaching seat instead of a roster spot keeps the Bulls' final open slot flexible.Word of the move spread fast around the league. Former teammates and organizations from Minnesota and New York, two stops where Gibson left a mark, praised both his staying power and his shift into coaching. That kind of respect travels, and it should help him now that his job is about accountability instead of minutes.His last stretch on the court was modest by design. Memphis signed him in February, played him in just 10 games, and got 3.4 points and 2.7 rebounds a night out of him. It wasn't about production at that point. He was the second-oldest active player in the league behind LeBron James, and teams wanted him around for what he brought off the stat sheet. articles.summary: NBA News: It has been a while but the wait is over. Kawhi Leonard is in the Toronto Raptors again, and the trade reuniting him with the franchise he led to a ch.
articles.body: It has been a while but the wait is over. Kawhi Leonard is in the Toronto Raptors again, and the trade reuniting him with the franchise he led to a championship in 2019 is no longer hypothetical. The Raptors and Clippers received league approval Monday to finalize the deal both sides shook hands on back in late June, ending a stretch where an already-completed trade sat frozen because of an active NBA investigation.Nothing about the trade package changed in the two and a half months it spent in limbo. The Clippers still get Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick and a stack of draft compensation, and the Raptors still get their franchise cornerstone back. What changed is the context: the NBA's probe into how the Clippers paid Leonard is now closed, complete with penalties that reshaped the roster math on both sides.CategoryDetailsPlayerKawhi LeonardFormer TeamLos Angeles ClippersNew TeamToronto RaptorsContract StatusFinal year of three-year, $103 million deal signed in 2019; extension expected with RaptorsClippers ReceiveBrandon Ingram, Gradey Dick, 2031 and 2033 unprotected first-round picks, 2027 first-round pick swap, 2030 and 2033 second-round picksOriginal AgreementJune 30League ApprovalMondayKawhi Leonard returns to Raptors from ClippersKawhi Leonard's return closes a loop that started when he left Toronto for the Clippers after that 2019 title run, still the only championship of his career.Raptors general manager Bobby Webster called it a statement move for a franchise trying to get back into contention, saying Leonard's "impact on our organization, our city and our country is undeniable."Leonard framed the moment as a reset after a turbulent offseason, saying he's "focused on what I can control, closing this chapter." At 35, he's coming off the best statistical season of his career, a career-high 27.9 points across 65 games for the Clippers last year, along with 6.4 rebounds and 3.6 assists.Kawhi Leonard's Clippers-Raptors trade detailsThe trade framework has been the same from what the two sides agreed in June. Toronto sends Leonard west and gets back a package built almost entirely on draft capital: two unprotected first-round picks in 2031 and 2033, a first-round pick swap in 2027, and second-round picks in 2030 and 2033.The Clippers get two rotation pieces in return. Ingram, extended to a three-year, $120 million deal shortly after Toronto acquired him, averaged 21.5 points, 4.8 rebounds and 3.7 assists last season. Dick, the Raptors' 2023 first-round pick, saw his role shrink, with his scoring dropping to 6.0 points per game on 30% 3-point shooting.Why was Kawhi Leonard's Clippers-Raptors trade delayed?The agreement sat frozen because the NBA was investigating whether the Clippers circumvented the salary cap when they signed Leonard to that three-year, $103 million deal in July 2019, reportedly including a no-show job worth $28 million. Both franchises agreed not to finalize the trade until the league closed its probe. The findings landed hard: Ballmer drew a one-year suspension and a $30 million fine, and the team forfeited five first-round picks. Leonard himself was fined $700,000, though the league didn't suspend him or void his contract. As for his fortune, Leonard is estimated to have earned approximately $375.8 million in NBA salary through the end of the 2026-27 season.Ballmer has already said he won't challenge the punishment. For Leonard, the next milestone is a contract extension with Toronto, something the Clippers weren't willing to offer. articles.title: Ex-USC basketball star Chad Baker-Mazara files lawsuit after split, claims coach Eric Musselman went on 'racially-charged tirade'
articles.summary: Chad Baker-Mazara split with USC before the Big Ten tournament last season, days after an alleged locker room incident.
articles.body:
Chad Baker-Mazara's departure from USC basketball last season came after head coach Eric Musselman went off on a "profanity-laced, racially-charged" tirade against him in the locker room, the former player is alleging in a new lawsuit.

Baker-Mazara filed a lawsuit in Los Angeles on Monday, according to the California Post , claiming that Musselman erupted on him after the team's loss to Nebraska on Feb. 28. Baker-Mazara and the Trojans split just days later. He is suing the university for breach of contract, conversion and intentional interference with prospective economic advantage, among other things.

Baker-Mazara left USC during the final stretch of the regular season. Specifics of his departure weren't known, other than it was reportedly due to "an accumulation of issues," but the timing was suspect. The announcement came on March 1, just days before the Trojans kicked off the Big Ten tournament.

Baker-Mazara transferred into USC from Auburn, and averaged career-highs of 18.5 points and 4.2 rebounds per game.

The incident in question, according to the lawsuit, happened after the Trojans' loss to Nebraska on Feb. 28. Baker-Mazara said that Musselman started yelling at the team in the locker room. Baker-Mazara tried to address his teammates, and Musselman shut him down.

"You shut the f**k up! You are one of the worst teammates anyone can ever have!" Musselman screamed at him, according to the lawsuit.

Baker-Mazara then asked Musselman if he should leave.

"Yes, leave!" Musselman allegedly responded. "Go back to the f***ing Dominican Republic! Nobody wants you here! F**k you!"

Baker-Mazara said in the lawsuit that he took those comments, as someone who was born in the Dominican Republic, similarly "to telling an African-American to 'go back to Africa.'"

"Coach Musselman's outburst was a direct attack on Baker-Mazara's national origin and Dominican heritage, made from a position of authority and power by the head coach of the team, in front of all of Baker-Mazara's teammates," the lawsuit said. "The tirade was unprovoked, vicious, and discriminatory."

Baker-Mazara also alleged that after his split with USC, the school terminated his NIL agreements and claimed that he had violated a "morals clause."

"The morals clause is hopelessly vague, overbroad, and unenforceable," the lawsuit said. "But in any event, reliance on the morals clause was entirely pretextual — a post hoc justification manufactured to allow USC to conserve its NIL funding pool and avoid paying the remaining substantial fixed sum owed to [Baker-Mazara] after the season had collapsed and Baker-Mazara's services could no longer take the Trojan basketball team where it wanted to go."

USC did not comment on the lawsuit to The Post.

Baker-Mazara was not selected in the NBA Draft earlier this year. He is expected to play professionally in Puerto Rico this season.

Musselman was hired to take over at USC ahead of the 2024-25 campaign after a five-year run at Arkansas. The Trojans went 18-14 last season and have yet to make the NCAA tournament under his watch.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham Says Next WNBA Commissioner Must ‘Unite Everybody’
articles.summary: Sophie Cunningham said the WNBA's next commissioner needs to unite the league and maintain an open line of communication with players.
articles.body:
Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham said Monday that the next WNBA commissioner needs to unite a league with "all types of walks" in it.

Cunningham spoke after Fever practice, in comments reported by Sporting News and posted on video by The Athletic's James Boyd. Cathy Engelbert announced Sept. 4 that she will retire at the end of the year, and her successor is expected to take over in 2027.

Getting to know players from other walks of life is part of what Cunningham enjoys about the league.

"The WNBA has always been a place for people to feel safe and comfortable," Cunningham said. "I think there are all types of walks in this league, which I think is absolutely awesome. But I think with that, you need someone who is going to unite everybody, because it can be so different."

Sophie Cunningham Wants Commissioner Who Can Unite WNBA

Cunningham has no candidate of her own. NBA commissioner Adam Silver is expected to make the hire, and ESPN reported that the search will begin later this month.

"God no. … I have talked to [NBA commissioner] Adam Silver a couple times," Cunningham said. "… I think he's gonna put someone in place who really wants to even take our league to another level."

Minnesota Lynx coach Cheryl Reeve, speaking Monday in Minneapolis, ruled herself out for the job.

WNBA Has Discussed Transgender Athlete Eligibility

In a July profile with ESPN , Cunningham said she opposes transgender girls and women competing in girls' and women's sports. She said she wanted to "protect biological women." Small rallies and protests followed at Fever road games in Seattle and Portland .

On Aug. 12, a WNBA task force of team executives met virtually to discuss transgender athlete eligibility and online vitriol directed at players. Engelbert had outlined the meeting in a memo to teams days earlier. The league said afterward that no immediate eligibility matter was before it.

League rules state that only players who are women are eligible to play in the WNBA. The rules do not define "women." There are no openly transgender players in the league.

Former NBA players Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White later declared for the 2027 WNBA draft, saying they identify as women. League sources told ESPN and The Associated Press that neither is eligible. Freedom has said he would drop his draft effort if the league limited eligibility explicitly to biological females.

On Aug. 23, Freedom was removed from a Fever game against the Chicago Sky at Wintrust Arena after a verbal altercation with Sky guard Natasha Cloud . He was sitting courtside in a shirt that read "WOMAN noun. adult human female." The Sky banned him indefinitely from home games.

Freedom filed a federal lawsuit Sept. 3 against the Sky, the city of Chicago, and the Metropolitan Pier and Exposition Authority, alleging his First Amendment rights were violated. Sky owner Michael Alter called the suit "meritless and frivolous."

Cunningham Wants Players-First Commissioner

Cunningham also said she wants a "players-first" commissioner. Players and the league reached a new collective bargaining agreement in March after negotiations that lasted nearly 18 months. Maximum contracts under the deal are worth $1.4 million this season.

Cunningham said the next commissioner will have to make hard decisions.

"If you have that open line of communication, that respect level, I think that it just feels different," Cunningham said.

Last week, Cunningham floated herself for the job on her podcast with co-host Drew Hanlen. She listed changes she would make, including a functional practice facility for every team, more respect between league management and players, more games, and more money.

"Honestly, the more I think about that, I think I should be the commissioner," Cunningham told Hanlen. "I think I could get this (expletive) on the right track. Let me tell you that."

In August, Cunningham told USA Today that the commissioner job could be open after this season and called for a leader who is "bold."

Indiana acquired Cunningham from the Phoenix Mercury in a four-team trade in February 2025.

The Fever are 26-14 and have clinched a playoff berth. With four games left, they sit fifth in the standings, and Atlanta holds the tiebreaker for fourth. Indiana is three games behind the Golden State Valkyries for second.

The Fever play the Toronto Tempo on Friday and then face the Washington Mystics . They close the regular season with two games against the Minnesota Lynx.

The Fever are 26-14 and have clinched a playoff berth. With four games left, they sit fifth in the standings, and Atlanta holds the tiebreaker for fourth. Indiana is three games behind the Golden State Valkyries for second.

The Fever play the Toronto Tempo on Friday and then face the Washington Mystics . They close the regular season with two games against the Minnesota Lynx.

articles.title: Mirotic, al Valencia Basket: el último pelotazo del baloncesto europeo
articles.standfirst: El ala-pívot de 35 años y 2,08 metros firma con el club taronja para la próxima temporada
articles.summary: El ala-pívot de 35 años y 2,08 metros firma con el club taronja para la próxima temporada
articles.body: El tremendo mercado veraniego del baloncesto europeo aún guardaba un último pelotazo. Lo ha protagonizado el Valencia Basket, que ha alcanzado un acuerdo con Nikola Mirotic. El ala-pívot de 35 años y 2,08 metros se ha comprometido con el club taronja para la próxima temporada después de desvincularse del AS Monaco, donde jugó el curso pasado con promedios de 11 puntos con un 39,3% en triples, 4,4 rebotes y 1,4 asistencias para 12,7 de valoración en 31 partidos de Euroliga. Aunque en las últimas semanas se había especulado con su retirada, el jugador montenegrino regresa a España, donde militó en el Real Madrid, club en el que se formó, en el Palencia, en condición de cedido, y en el Barcelona. Al club azulgrana llegó en un mediático fichaje por su pasado madridista y tras una aventura en la NBA que duró de 2014 a 2019. Allí jugó en los Bulls, los Pelicans y los Bucks. Salió del Palau en 2023 rumbo a Milán, después pasó por Mónaco y ahora regresa a la Liga Endesa. Mirotic es un clásico de la Euroliga, competición en la que suma 12 temporadas, aunque en la de su estreno sólo disputó dos minutos. A lo largo de 307 encuentros sus promedios son de 14,4 puntos con un 39,9% en triples, 5,2 rebotes y 1,2 asistencias y 17,1 créditos de valoración. Es el quinto jugador más valorado tras Mike James, Nando De Colo, Kostas Sloukas y Jan Vesely y el quinto máximo anotador de la historia del torneo sólo por detrás de los tres primeros citados y Vassilis Spanoulis. Su espina, haber alcanzado seis veces la Final Four y no haber podido levantar el cetro continental. En su palmarés cuenta con 15 títulos. Entre ellos tres Ligas Endesa, dos con el Barça y una con el Madrid, una Liga italiana y otra francesa y cuatro Copas ACB repartidas entre su etapa blanca y la azulgrana. Internacional con la selección española conquistó el oro en el Eurobasket de 2015 y el bronce en los Juegos Olímpicos de Río en 2016. Mirotic completa la reconstrucción del Valencia Basket, que ha sido casi absoluta este verano. Es el décimo fichaje del equipo taronja, que ha tenido que reinventarse tras la marcha del entrenador Pedro Martínez y de jugadores clave como Jean Montero, Jaime Pradilla, Brancou Badio y Braxton Key. Todos ellos fueron fundamentales para ganar la Liga Endesa y alcanzar la Final Four de la Euroliga por primera vez en la historia de la entidad. Junto al montenegrino han llegado Mario Saint-Supery, T.J. Shorts, Armoni Brooks, Gonzalo Corbalán, Lucas Marí, Elias Valtonen, Dylan Osetkowski, Mo Gueye y Jasiel Rivero, aunque este con un contrato temporal. Importantes refuerzos para intentar hacer olvidar a los ídolos marchados y acercarse a los éxitos de la campaña pasada.

articles.title: La venganza de 'Il Gallo' de la NBA: "Kawhi me metió en un lío; él debería pagar esos 50 millones"
articles.standfirst: Gallinari no olvida que "Kawhi Leonard cambió la trayectoria de mi carrera; me puso en una situación difícil al enviarme lejos de Los Ángeles. Shai y yo pagamos el precio"
articles.summary: Gallinari no olvida que "Kawhi Leonard cambió la trayectoria de mi carrera; me puso en una situación difícil al enviarme lejos de Los Ángeles. Shai y yo pagamos el precio"
articles.body: Danilo Gallinari, jugador italiano con tres lustros de experiencia en la NBA, se mostró muy duro con Kawhi Leonard tras la resolución del escándalo de Los Angeles Clippers y ajustó cuentas por una antigua cuita con el nuevo jugador de los Toronto Raptors. "Esos malditos 50 millones, de los cuales él solo tiene que pagar 700.000... en mi opinión, debería pagarlos todos", declaró 'Il Gallo' en su podcast 'A Crest Alta' tras la sanción de la NBA a los Clippers por eludir las normas del tope salarial al facilitar acuerdos comerciales entre Leonard y empresas vinculadas a la franquicia californiana. Los Clippers deben pagar una multa de 30 millones de dólares, pierden cinco selecciones de primera ronda del Draft y su propietario Steve Ballmer ha sido suspendido un año. Por su parte Kawhi Leonard debe pagar 700.000 dólares de multa. Danilo Gallinari no se olvida que en 2019 salió de los Clippers tras el fichaje de Kawhi Leonard, que acababa de ganar la NBA con Toronto y pidió al equipo angelino que armara un equipo capaz de luchar por el campeonato de inmediato. Los Clippers adquirieron a Paul George procedente de los Thunder a cambio de Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, cinco selecciones de primera ronda de Draft y Gallinari, quien venía de completar su mejor temporada en la NBA con un promedio de 19,8 puntos. "Kawhi Leonard cambió la trayectoria de mi carrera; me puso en una situación difícil al enviarme lejos de Los Ángeles. Al final, Shai y yo fuimos quienes pagamos el precio", recuerda el italiano. Danilo Gallinari quiso subrayar que no le guarda rencor a Kawhi Leonard: "En realidad, ambos terminamos recorriendo caminos maravillosos, porque aquel año en Oklahoma City fue increíble". "Mi carrera en la NBA no fue moldeada por un manager general o un propietario —como había sucedido con los Knicks—, sino por un jugador que decidió que el equipo no era lo suficientemente bueno y quería otra cosa", recordó. Danilo Gallinari matizó que "Kawhi Leonard no debería darme ese dinero a mí, sino destinarlo a obras benéficas. Sin embargo, tiene que pagar la suma completa sin falta".

articles.title: Building the NBA's All-Overpaid Team Ahead of 2026-27 Season
articles.summary: As we set out on our annual journey to build the NBA's All-Overpaid team ahead of 2026-27 training camps, it's important to remember this won't be a step-for-step repeat of the league's worst contracts.
articles.body:
As we set out on our annual journey to build the NBA's All-Overpaid team ahead of 2026-27 training camps, it's important to remember this won't be a step-for-step repeat of the league's worst contracts .

A compilation of the least team-friendly deals considers the length of an entire agreement. Our All-Overpaid squad cares only about how much on-court value we can expect players to provide relative to their 2026-27 salaries alone.

This approach opens the door for expiring-contract names to make the First Team cut. More importantly, it is why you shouldn't expect to see players such as Donovan Mitchell or Devin Booker, whose mammoth pay grades aren't imminently problematic.

Final nominations will follow a conventional lineup structure: two guards, two forwards and a center.

Though selections are made independently, we'll be using a model developed by the Sporting News' Steph Noh to offer a window into every player's " salary surplus ."

To reach that number, we'll assume each player averages as many minutes as they did last season while making at least 60 appearances or matching their average number of games played over the past three years—whichever is higher. The figures that Noh's model spits out will show us how much every selection is overpaid.

Guard: Ja Morant, Portland Trail Blazers

Availability warts coupled with a highly questionable roster fit make Ja Morant a necessary selection over fellow high-paid guards like De'Aaron Fox and Trae Young.

Ignoring the games-played problem is a non-starter. Morant has made just 79 appearances over the past three seasons. The reasons for his absences vary, covering injuries, suspensions and the Memphis Grizzlies' direction. But missing more than two-thirds of regular-season tilts for this long strips away the benefit of the doubt from your person, no matter what.

Better availability isn't a cure-all, either. Morant's rim frequency has been in steady decline for years, which is usually a harbinger of ebbing athleticism.

The path to recalibrating his game is, at best, unclear. He is a career 31.1 percent shooter from long range, doesn't have a ton of experience working outside a ball-dominant role and adds no value to the defensive end.

All of this becomes exponentially more problematic on the Portland Trail Blazers. They remain in desperate need of shooting, even with Damian Lillard set to play next season, and can't sustain Morant's on-ball usage without reorienting the roles of Deni Avdija, Scoot Henderson and Jrue Holiday.

This is the seedy underbelly of Portland's dice roll. It didn't give up a ton to get Morant; just Jerami Grant and Kris Murray. But it's now left to shell out 25-plus percent of the cap for a player whose best-case outcome won't come without collateral damage.

Christian Braun is young enough with the hustle-culture track record for this selection to look silly. You can also close your eyes, pick someone at random and find a player, many times over, with a much larger "overpaid by" projection.

Still, Braun remains the most unsettling kind of offensive wild card.

Already a low-volume three-point shooter, he saw his above-the-break efficiency last season plunge by 17 percentage points—the second-largest drop by any non-big who played at least 500 minutes, according to BBall Index. This would be easier, albeit still difficult, to write off if Braun's dependence on Nikola Jokić was traveling in the right direction.

Across both the regular season and playoffs last year, Braun's two-point percentage nosedived by 28 points without the three-time MVP on the floor. He also posted a 31.8 true shooting percentage overall on self-created attempts—a career-worst mark that ranked in the 24th percentile leaguewide.

Dedicating this large of a salary to such a limited offensive player almost never turns out well. And when looking at how shallow and hard up for shooting the Nuggets remain, they will feel the ramifications more than most.

Second Team Guards: Jalen Green, Phoenix Suns; Jordan Poole, New Orleans Pelicans

Certain members of the Boston Celtics' propagandist machine have started asking some variation of: What does Jaylen Brown actually do better at basketball than Paul George?

Congrats to those pretzel-twisters for looking at select shooting slashes and pick-and-roll numbers. But there are more than a few answers , the most important of which is: Jaylen Brown regularly plays basketball at all.

George has missed fewer than 15 games just once since 2018-19. And over that span, he has averaged over 30 absences per season. Counting on better health as he enters year 17, at age 36, verges on unhinged. It also guarantees nothing.

Playing more doesn't mean his effectiveness won't taper off. Whether he closes 2025-26 as strong as he did without a 25-game suspension giving him time to refresh is one of last season's great what-ifs.

Never mind what George does better or as well as Brown. Tethering almost 33 percent of your cap to this amount of raw uncertainty doesn't typically end well. It just seems nobody told Boston.

Forward: Patrick Williams, Chicago Bulls

Is it OK if you have a combo forward making $18 million who's projected to be overpaid by $18 million? We're asking for the Chicago Bulls.

Patrick Williams' issues need no introduction. He has never developed into a plug-and-pay offensive force, and his defense has topped out at "reasonable enough, if you squint hard enough."

Pick a catch-all metric. Any catch-all metric . If Williams has ever ranked better than 300th in it during a single season, screenshot it, print it out, frame it and send it to his agent.

Believe it or not, there's a chance Williams looks even more overpaid this season.

Chicago's new front office regime, led by Bryson Graham, has no draft or sweat equity invested in him. With Matas Buzelis, Caleb Wilson, Dailyn Swain and Leonard Miller all on the roster, there's a strong chance, if not inevitability, Williams spends more time outside the Bulls' rotation than in it.

Second Team Forwards: Nikola Jović, Miami Heat; Jerami Grant, Memphis Grizzlies

Joel Embiid's "overpaid by" number is actually a gift. It rests on him appearing in 60 games—something he hasn't come close to doing since 2022.

Even if he's healthy, the Philadelphia 76ers could max him out at 45 or 50 games in hopes of preserving him for the playoffs. Lower than 60-game threshold by 10, and his "overpaid by" projection rises to nearly $25 million.

Any path to leaving Embiid off this list has to begin with "Look at what he can do when he's actually healthy!" But even that pipe-dream argument has lost steam.

To his credit, after shedding weight last year, Embiid appears to have slimmed down further. That could boost his on-court mobility and longevity. And yet, the fact we're having this conversation about the sixth-highest-paid player in the league says it all. His pay grade is under water, and it has no chance of coming up for air.

Second Team Center: Jakob Poeltl, Toronto Raptors

Dan Favale is a National NBA Writer for Bleacher Report. Follow him on Bluesky ( @danfavale ), and subscribe to the Hardwood Knocks podcast, co-hosted by Bleacher Report's Grant Hughes .

articles.title: Nebraska continues to climb in USA TODAY Sports NCAA Re-Rank
articles.summary: USA TODAY Sports released its week 2 NCAA Re-Rank. Nebraska moved up for the second week in a row, now sitting at No. 37.
articles.body:
USA TODAY Sports released its week two NCAA Re-Rank 1-138 on Monday. Nebraska moved up for the second week in a row, now sitting at No. 37.

The Huskers jumped three spots from last week, and six from the start of the season, following a 2-0 start and a wild weekend of play. Now only three opponents on Nebraska's schedule sit in the top 25: No. 4 Indiana , No. 6 Ohio State and No. 23 Iowa . Washington (No. 29) and Oregon (No. 30) both dropped out of the top 25. The Huskies held out against Utah State 16-14. The Ducks suffered a 39-31 upset loss at Oklahoma State.

Illinois also drifted down in the rankings, going from No. 41 to No. 46 after a 31-27 loss to Duke. USC (No. 8), Penn State (No. 16) and Michigan (No. 18) are other Big Ten teams ranked ahead of the Huskers. Texas now stands at No. 1 after taking down Ohio State, jumping over Notre Dame (No. 2) to grab the spot.

Nebraska concludes its non-conference stretch on Saturday night against North Dakota. Kickoff is set for 6:15 p.m. CT on BTN.

articles.title: Pau Gasol: "La selección femenina me recuerda a la nuestra de 2006"
articles.standfirst: La leyenda del deporte español participa en un torneo de golf a favor de la Gasol Foundation y de la mano del Santander Private Banking
articles.summary: La leyenda del deporte español participa en un torneo de golf a favor de la Gasol Foundation y de la mano del Santander Private Banking
articles.body: Pau Gasol acaba de participar en un torneo de golf solidario a favor de Gasol Foundation y de la mano de Santander Private Banking. Al evento, celebrado en el Club de Golf Santander de Boadilla del Monte, se sumaron algunos referentes históricos del deporte español como el exfutbolista Raúl González y el exjugador de baloncesto, Sergio Rodríguez. Pau todavía saboreaba el gran papel de la selección femenina en el Mundial. "Es un equipo muy especial. Me recuerda a la nuestra". El torneo solidario, organizado junto al Santander en una iniciativa "que sume", como le gusta decir al catalán, sirve para promover las actividades de la fundación que preside junto a su hermano Marc: promoción de la salud infantil y reducción de las desigualdades. Pau confesó tener un hándicap 10,6 y recordó que para mejorar en el golf "hay que trabajar mucho. Es un deporte que tiene de todo, hay que relajarse y disfrutar, pero también emplear mucho tiempo si quieres prosperar". La leyenda del deporte español, casi recién aterrizado procedente de Berlín, se mostró encantado con la progresión del deporte femenino, como se pudo ver en el reciente Mundial de Baloncesto. Al mismo tiempo, celebró el empuje de la selección femenina. "Fue una experiencia muy bonita. El deporte femenino está creciendo y en auge, subiendo el listón cada año, y el Mundial ha dado un paso adelante en todos los sentidos. Se está generando un movimiento fuente en torno al deporte femenino y nuestra selección lo ha hecho muy bien. Tenemos un equipo joven de gran nivel con el que podemos seguir construyendo. Me recuerda a nuestra selección de 2006. Vi muy buen ambiente, muy buena química, muy buena compenetración. Sentí una gran cohesión como equipo". Pau destacó el papel de muchas jugadoras, especialmente Iyana Martín, que esta temporada, antes de dar el salto a la WNBA, jugará en el Girona, club del que es vicepresidente. "Es una selección ilusionante de grandísimo nivel. Iyana es muy especial, Awa va a seguir desarrollándose y va a ser muy dominante. Veo a un grupo muy cohesionado. María y Raquel han jugado a un gran nivel. Me gustó mucho que Alba, cuyo papel fue fundamental, estuviera otra vez para sumar otra medalla". El presidente de la Comisión de Atletas del COI también habló de los Juegos de Los Ángeles 2028. Está dentro del movimiento olímpico y conoce de primera mano la ciudad, tras su paso por los Lakers. "Van a ser muy especiales y punteros. Van a tener un nivel comercial y organizativo muy alto. Para un deportista los Juegos es lo máximo. Es nuestra competición favorita".
